def test(page):
    page.goto("http://app:8000/")
    page.expect_image("start", region=[0, 128, 360, 212], precondition=True)
    page.click(360, 500)
    page.type_text("Bring the blue notebook.")
    page.click(569, 170)
    page.reload()
    page.expect_image("start", region=[0, 128, 360, 212], precondition=True)
    page.expect_image("reopened", region=[0, 128, 720, 400])

content.text:
I saved the test to `/workspace/output/test.py`. I haven't run it, because there's no way to execute Python while authoring.

In the live app I tapped into the empty `atlas` note, typed `Bring the blue notebook.` and tapped Save. After a reload the text was still showing, and the undo and save icons had greyed out.

The test does the same steps:
1. It opens the app and checks that the title bar region (the `atlas` header, left part) matches the `start` reference.
2. It taps the editor, types the text and taps Save.
3. It reloads the app and checks the title bar again.
4. It compares the top of the screen, covering the title bar and the note text, to the `reopened` reference.

That last check is the behavioural assertion: the text must be visible after reopening.

I deliberately left the bottom edge of the screen out of the comparison. A thin progress bar appeared there right after the reload, and I judged it transient. I didn't confirm that it goes away, so the comparison region is a guess about what stays stable.
